One way to approach this is to recognize that your reflex to guard what it loves can sometimes become a mental process of defending your own interpretation. When this happens, you might wonder if you're protecting your understanding of the situation, rather than the core needs or values it represents.

It's possible that the missing part of the conflict is not as unknown as it seems. Your Baseline suggests that you hold and protect what matters, which means you care deeply about the underlying issues. You might be more interested in understanding the dynamics than in guessing what the other side might be thinking.

Consider if you could separate the information you have from the story you've made up about the missing part. This distinction can help you identify the gaps in your knowledge and what you can do differently in the future.
